page: Amazon Web Services r6i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance delivers 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Memory bandwidth benchmarks record 149.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 68.49 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached small-block reads achieve 1672.87 GB/sec. The instance provides 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no local instance storage or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations position the r6i.8xlarge in the average performance tier across general compute metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 36549.21, a Geekbench multi-core score of 13944.0, and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 30971.18. In in-memory data testing, it handles 30.96 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database score of 14652.18. While small model LLM text generation shows strong results at 302.47 tokens per second, large model prompt processing slows to 6.15 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

This server represents a balanced resource density profile for enterprise architectures that demand high RAM availability without requiring extreme compute acceleration. It is primarily matched to memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise database management systems, big data analytics engines, and large-scale data caching layers.
